Name: escaped_markup_judges_format_spoofing
Title: Escaped Markup: Preventing Verdict Spoofing in Structured Multimodal LLM Judges
Short Hypothesis: Appending a non-imperative verdict-spoof suffix that imitates the judge's reserved markup (e.g., \boxed{Response X is better}) will cause substantial attack success on structured multimodal judges, and a training-free reserved-token escaping wrapper will reduce attack success by a large margin with minimal clean-accuracy loss.
Related Work: PhyCritic (Xiong et al., 2026) trains a multimodal critic using structured prompts with \boxed{} verdicts. VL-RewardBench (CVPR 2025) benchmarks multimodal preference judges. JudgeDeceiver shows optimization-based suffix attacks flip judge preferences. Spotlighting (2024) proposes encoding transformations for prompt injection defense. GCG (Zou et al., 2023) introduces gradient-based adversarial suffix generation. No prior work specifically evaluates \boxed{} verdict spoofing attacks on structured multimodal judges or proposes reserved-sequence escaping as a defense.

Experiment Plan.model: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (~14GB on RTX 5080) + Gemini for cross-model testing
